description: A group of two working on biology and software.
summary: Project Elysium is an offline-first PHP web application engineered to support astronaut self-assessment during long-duration missions. Addressing the Human Research Program’s hazards of isolation, altered gravity, and closed environments, the app guides crew members through a daily "Periodic Health Status" (PHS) check-in for vital signs, sleep, and mood, alongside an afternoon log for precise nutrition and exercise countermeasures. To prevent data overload, a rules-based triage engine automatically correlates inputs (e.g., poor sleep combined with elevated heart rate) to generate actionable warnings and flight surgeon contact criteria. The interface features a gamified XP and streak system to maintain daily health habits, an educational interactive body map detailing spaceflight physiological risks, and a robust hybrid storage architecture that caches data locally to ensure uninterrupted operation even if server communication is lost.
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

Project Elysium is an offline-first, self-assessment dashboard tailored for long-duration spaceflight. It operates on a dual-loop daily routine: a morning Periodic Health Status (PHS) check (logging mood, sleep, heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, and temperature) and an afternoon Daily Log (tracking exact meals and exercise countermeasures).

The core of Elysium is a rules-based assessment engine. As astronauts input data, the system compares it against terrestrial reference ranges and their own 14-day rolling baselines. It categorizes overall health into four states: Normal, Watch, Attention, and Not Assessed. If it detects compounding issues (e.g., short sleep, elevated heart rate, and low mood), it triggers a "correlation warning" and provides specific, actionable countermeasures (like breathing exercises) or clear thresholds for contacting a flight surgeon. It also features an interactive body map that dynamically updates based on telemetry, explaining the physiological risks of spaceflight for each body system.

What benefits does it have?

  • Triage and Early Warning: Instead of just collecting data, Elysium interprets it. It catches subtle, compounding health trends (like sleep debt leading to cardiovascular strain) before they become critical.
  • Habit Formation via Gamification: Built-in XP, level-ups, and daily streaks incentivize astronauts to maintain strict health-monitoring routines, reducing the cognitive burden of remembering to log data.
  • Communication Delay Resilience: Spacecraft and Martian rovers face communication blackouts and latency. Elysium utilizes a hybrid storage architecture—saving locally to the browser and syncing to the PHP server asynchronously—ensuring astronauts are never blocked from logging critical health data.
  • Medical Education: The "Body View" provides "just-in-time" training, explaining what certain measurements mean, how spaceflight hazards (like microgravity and radiation) affect those systems, and when a symptom warrants medical intervention.

What is the intended impact of the project?

The primary impact of Project Elysium is astronaut autonomy and safety. As missions extend to the Moon and Mars, astronauts cannot rely on real-time guidance from Earth. Elysium acts as a digital flight surgeon, empowering crew members to confidently assess their own health, make immediate lifestyle corrections, and recognize when a situation requires urgent medical consultation. It shifts the paradigm from reactive medicine to proactive, data-driven wellness.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Backend: PHP (for session management and server-side JSON state persistence).
  • Frontend: Vanilla HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript (ES6+). No heavy frameworks (React/Vue) were used to ensure Elysium remains lightweight, fast, and capable of running on low-bandwidth spacecraft networks.
  • APIs: HTML5 Canvas API (used to render real-time animated ECG and plethysmogram traces), Web Storage API (for offline-first LocalStorage caching), and the Fetch API (for asynchronous, debounced server syncing).
  • Design: Custom CSS variables for instant light/dark mode switching, native SVG for scalable UI icons, and CSS animations for micro-feedback (ripples, toasts, and XP floating text).

How is your project creative?

  • Conversational UI: Instead of a cold spreadsheet, the health check-in is presented as a chat interface. It feels natural, guides the user step-by-step, and delivers medical advice contextually.
  • "Tactile" Feedback: The UI is packed with micro-interactions. Saving a meal triggers a green flash and a toast notification; logging a metric awards floating XP; expanding the vitals card reveals a beautifully animated, simulated real-time heartbeat. This makes health logging feel engaging rather than tedious.
  • Context-Aware Architecture: Elysium changes its behavior based on the time of day and what has been logged. It won't ask for nutrition at 6:00 AM, and it automatically locks PHS tasks until they are complete before moving to the daily log.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Cognitive Load: Astronauts are extremely busy. The check-in flow is intentionally split into "Morning" and "Afternoon" to prevent survey fatigue, and the UI uses high-contrast, color-coded badges (Green, Yellow, Red) so health status can be parsed at a glance.
  • Medical Safety: We explicitly avoided hard-coding medical diagnoses. Elysium uses the phrases "Watch" and "Attention" and consistently reminds the user that terrestrial reference ranges are being used, always deferring final judgment to a human flight surgeon.
  • Hostile Environments: We considered the harsh reality of spaceflight software. Elysium is designed to be fully functional without an internet connection, operating strictly on local cache and syncing in the background when the network allows.
  • Accessibility: We factored in varying lighting conditions inside a spacecraft by implementing a seamless Dark Mode/Light Mode toggle, and ensured keyboard navigability (tab indexes) for all interactive elements.
